posts.title: Software you can argue with
posts.description: Picture this; you're standing at McDonalds and there's no way to get rid of the pickles. It's an every day problem with software. There a diminishing return to options, and yours just happen to be dim. But in the near future, that UI is an agent. So you'll be able to tell it "hey I don't want any pickles, can you do that?" and it will. Very soon, every touch point between systems, and between peop

posts.title: Organisations dropping tasks
posts.description: This is a bit of an extreme idea, but hear me out. It's the norm today that companies optimise for time so much they routinely drop tasks. There are queues, support tickets that go stale, projects that never ship. We see it in our daily lives as well, the todolist just grows, the home renovation is never complete. We're so used to this, it feels normal. It feels like this is the way it has to be.

posts.title: Dangerous technology
posts.description: The latest news in the AI hype cycle is that Dario is convincing all the frontier labs to slow down because AI is too dangerous to release. The Playstation 2 was export-controlled because it was a super computer that could be used to make nuclear weapons . All technology is dangerous, from scissors to cyanide. Lets stop pretending otherwise and get on with it.
